saying: all come from dust, and all return to dust
source: Drawn from the BSB, STEPBible TAHOT and TAGNT, and the commentaries named under each note.

layers.evidence: Rests on the verse's plain words about the grave and the dust.
layers.text: People and animals end up in the same place, the grave. All were formed from the dust, and at death all their bodies go back to the dust.

layers.evidence: The Companion Bible points the phrase turn to dust again to Genesis 3:19, and Keil-Delitzsch compare Genesis 3:19 directly. Both verses use afar (dust) and shuv (return).
layers.text: The words all come from dust, and all return to dust echo God's sentence on Adam after the first sin: For dust you are, and to dust you shall return (Genesis 3:19). The same Hebrew words for dust (afar) and return (shuv) are used.
